topic: Study a two-arm randomized recurrent-event trial with absorbing death and right censoring, fixed switch time k, clinical cap H>=2, and a finite event-count threshold menu M. Retain the Janvin C2-C6 causal conditions but DEFINE capped no-carry-over as the replacement for raw C7: for intensive survivors, baseline capped burden B and switched residual W have identified marginals and obey B+W<=H. Characterize the resulting Ferrers transport polytope by exact Hall inequalities and a constructive coupling. Derive sharp fixed-threshold endpoints including the backward-deficit upper CDF; prove every compatible triple coupling has an observed-law-preserving finite-history causal response-tree lift; identify the complete joint threshold-value set; compute support functions, pairwise worst-case regret, and minimax thresholds with the eligibility-greedy O(H log H) algorithm; and give censoring-adjusted simultaneous confidence-polytope inversion covering the whole value set and all robust optimizers at Hall and policy ties. Include a concrete H=3 rational example where shared-law regret selects threshold 1 but separate marginal intervals select threshold 3. Treat SPRINT's published k=300 adverse-event switching analysis as a capped-loss consumer only if a clinically defensible cap can be prespecified. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Exact endpoint proofs, a full-history response-tree construction, and an eligibility-greedy support algorithm were derived. Exact rational checks passed 2,500 endpoint comparisons and 2,100 greedy-versus-LP comparisons, both gated witnesses, and the recommendation-reversal regret matrix. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Establish a clinically defensible cumulative cap H for which capped-increment no-carry-over is substantively credible in SPRINT, and independently formalize the finite-history causal lift and dual Lipschitz details. EARLY KILL TEST: For externally justified caps at k=300, compute censoring-adjusted Hall slacks and confidence-polytope feasibility, then compare shared-law regret with fixed m=1 and interval-box decisions; reject the SPRINT application if no defensible cap is credible or the model is statistically incompatible. open_problems.open_problem: What are the exact feasibility conditions and sharp distributional bounds for the switched total burden B+W when the identified integer-valued marginals of B and W must be coupled subject to B+W≤H?

source_refs.claim: The paper bounds an unsupported one-time treatment-switching estimand using no carry-over and marginal recurrent-count distributions, but does not impose or characterize a finite total-burden cap.
source_refs.author: Matias Janvin, Pål C. Ryalen, Aaron L. Sarvet, Mats J. Stensrud

source_refs.claim: The paper resolves sharpness subtleties for CDF bounds of sums with fixed marginals, especially for discrete distributions, but does not include the support restriction B+W≤H.
source_refs.author: Zhehao Zhang, Thomas S. Richardson

source_refs.claim: Strassen gives general existence criteria for couplings with prescribed marginals and constrained support, without the finite Ferrers specialization or causal endpoint formulas required here.
source_refs.author: Volker Strassen

open_problems.why_unsolved: Janvin et al.'s switching argument supplies the causal marginals, while classical sum bounds optimize over an unrestricted Fréchet class. The cap deletes every cell above the antidiagonal b+w=H, so unrestricted Makarov formulas need not remain sharp and marginal compatibility itself becomes nontrivial. The first missing step is to reduce Strassen's general subset inequalities to a complete finite family for this Ferrers support graph, then construct couplings attaining both ordinary and backward-looking CDF endpoints. Searches found the causal switching and constrained-coupling ingredients separately, but no capped recurrent-event specialization.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact finite Hall-inequality characterization of nonemptiness, an explicit coupling construction, and closed-form sharp lower and upper CDF bounds for B+W at every integer threshold, including the discrete backward-CDF correction.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the exact unsupported-switching motivation and presents weak assumptions and partial identification as the response to positivity failure.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A randomized trial observes no cross-arm switches -> conventional dynamic-regime positivity fails -> no-carry-over identifies relevant marginals -> a clinically bounded replacement requires a new constrained-coupling analysis

method_exemplars.technique: Specialize support-constrained coupling existence to the antidiagonal Ferrers relation and prove that its nested neighborhoods reduce the general subset conditions to prefix Hall inequalities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired identified set is exactly a class of probability measures with fixed marginals supported on B+W≤H.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the discrete extremal-coupling constructions and careful distinction between strict and weak CDF events when deriving attainable sum bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The capped counts are discrete, and the requested backward-CDF endpoint has the same atom-sensitive sharpness issue.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate the landmark recurrent-count and survival marginals with coarsening-at-random identification, stacked efficient influence functions, and multiply robust nuisance estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Those censoring-adjusted marginal cell probabilities are the inputs to every Hall slack and sharp capped endpoint.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the joint identified set of all threshold-policy values under one shared capped coupling, and how should pairwise worst-case regret and a deterministic minimax threshold be computed without replacing that set by marginal intervals?

source_refs.claim: The paper defines value and regret for threshold switching regimes and analyzes SPRINT at m=1, but does not characterize the joint value vector generated by one common latent coupling across a finite threshold menu.
source_refs.author: Matias Janvin, Pål C. Ryalen, Aaron L. Sarvet, Mats J. Stensrud

source_refs.claim: The paper shows that treatment choice under partial identification can have nonunique minimax-regret rules and that the geometry of the joint payoff restrictions matters.
source_refs.author: José Luis Montiel Olea, Chen Qiu, Jörg Stoye

source_refs.claim: The paper derives optimal decision rules when a point-identified law restricts a jointly partially identified payoff vector, rather than treating each action's interval independently.
source_refs.author: Timothy Christensen, Hyungsik Roger Moon, Frank Schorfheide

open_problems.why_unsolved: Each threshold value is a linear functional of the same latent transport plan, so its coordinates generally cannot attain their separate extrema simultaneously. Interval-by-interval regret therefore enlarges Nature's choice set and can select a different threshold. The unresolved step is to characterize the linear image of the Ferrers transport polytope and optimize value differences over it without running an unrelated linear program for every ordered pair. Searches found no shared-coupling analysis for recurrent-event threshold regimes.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact polyhedral description or support-function oracle for the complete threshold-value vector, formulas for every pairwise worst-case regret, and a proved polynomial-time algorithm returning the full deterministic minimax-threshold correspondence.

writing_exemplar.why: Its physician-facing threshold-switching formulation is the destination problem; the new work should preserve that arc while exposing dependence across candidate thresholds.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Early recurrent events motivate switching -> weak assumptions give ambiguous policy values -> several thresholds must be compared -> valid regret must respect their common latent law

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the minimax-regret game and profiled-regret comparison to a convex, jointly feasible vector of threshold payoffs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested object is a treatment-choice game over a set-identified payoff vector, with the transport image supplying the joint restriction.

method_exemplars.technique: Use regularized support-function estimation and its uniform Gaussian approximation for polygonal identified sets with changing active faces.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Worst-case value and regret are support functions of the joint value polytope, including at flat faces and ties.

open_problems.open_problem: Under the finite-history FFRCISTG model for recurrent-event switching, does every observed-law-compatible capped triple coupling admit a global response-tree realization without adding unintended cross-world independence?

source_refs.claim: FFRCISTG and SWIG models encode consistency and single-world independences while deliberately imposing fewer cross-world restrictions than NPSEM-IE models.
source_refs.author: Thomas S. Richardson, James M. Robins
source_refs.venue: University of Washington CSSS Working Paper 128

source_refs.claim: The structural causal marginal problem asks when separately specified marginal SCMs can be merged into one counterfactually consistent causal model.
source_refs.author: Luigi Gresele, Julius von Kügelgen, Jonas M. Kübler, Elke Kirschbaum, Bernhard Schölkopf, Dominik Janzing

source_refs.claim: A causal marginal polytope enforces local marginal compatibility without itself guaranteeing a global causal-model realization.
source_refs.author: Jakob Zeitler, Ricardo Silva

open_problems.why_unsolved: A feasible coupling establishes compatibility of selected counterfilhoactual summaries, not automaticallyIBLE a full process satisfying temporal order, consistency, treatment randomization, right-censoring structure, and absorption by death. Generic response-function encodings may silently strengthen the model to NPSEM-IE. The first missing step is an explicit history-by-history extension whose observed-data pushforward is unchanged and whose independence audit invokes only the intended FFRCISTG restrictions. Searches found general causal-marginal gluing machinery but no such recurrent-event switching lift.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A constructive map from every feasible capped triple law to a finite FFRCISTG response tree, with a converse, exact observed-law preservation, death-absorption verification, and an inventory of all induced cross-world restrictions.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames local-to-global counterfactual consistency as the central mathematical problem rather than assuming that compatible marginals automatically glue.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Several causal marginals may each be valid -> their overlaps can still be globally inconsistent -> sharp capped switching bounds require an explicit global causal realization

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate finite deterministic response types, mix them on a simplex, and verify observational and counterfactual constraints through their pushforwards.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested lift is a finite response-function witness inducing prescribed factual and switching-world margins.

method_exemplars.technique: Use SWIG node splitting and FFRCISTG single-world factorization to audit consistency and conditional independence at every history.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target realization must satisfy FFRCISTG specifically, without importing NPSEM-IE cross-world independence.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt categorical structural-causal-marginal gluing to the overlapping factual, continued-treatment, and switched-treatment margins.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly studies existence of a global SCM from prescribed marginal causal models.

open_problems.open_problem: Can censoring-adjusted inference cover the entire Hall-defined threshold-value polytope and the full minimax-threshold correspondence uniformly over binding Hall constraints and policy-value ties?

source_refs.claim: The SPRINT analysis uses a one-sided bootstrap confidence bound for one upper endpoint at m=1, rather than simultaneous inference for a joint value set or all robust optimizers.
source_refs.author: Matias Janvin, Pål C. Ryalen, Aaron L. Sarvet, Mats J. Stensrud

source_refs.claim: Criterion inversion yields confidence regions for identified sets defined by moment equalities and inequalities.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Han Hong, Elie Tamer

source_refs.claim: Generalized moment selection provides uniformly size-controlled inference when the binding subset of inequalities is unknown.
source_refs.author: Donald W. K. Andrews, Gustavo Soares

source_refs.claim: Regularized support-function estimation gives uniformly valid inference for polygonal affine identified sets at changing active faces.
source_refs.author: Bulat Gafarov

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing moment-inequality procedures do not automatically propagate recurrent-event censoring nuisance estimation through a random transport polytope and then through a set-valued minimax argmin. Hall ties change the active face of the identified set, while policy ties make single-valued optimizer selection discontinuous. The first missing proof step is a uniform joint expansion for every estimated marginal cell and Hall slack that remains valid when multiple constraints bind simultaneously.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A confidence-polytope inversion procedure with uniform asymptotic coverage of the complete joint causal value set and simultaneous outer coverage of every minimax threshold under arbitrary Hall and policy ties.

writing_exemplar.why: It organizes inference around coverage of the identified set itself, which is the correct framing for the transport-valued target.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Weak causal assumptions identify a set -> sampling error requires confidence regions for that set -> policy use additionally requires simultaneous coverage of its robust-optimizer image

method_exemplars.technique: Apply generalized moment selection and bootstrap critical values to the finite Hall system with an unknown binding set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Hall feasibility is a finite moment-inequality problem whose nonregular cases occur when slacks vanish.

method_exemplars.technique: Regularize estimated support functions and use the resulting uniform Gaussian approximation across polygon faces.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The value set is a polygonal linear image, and its endpoints and regret coordinates are support-function evaluations.

method_exemplars.technique: Stack efficient influence functions for landmark recurrent-count and survival marginals and approximate their joint law with a multiplier process.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Every Hall inequality is a linear function of those censoring-adjusted marginal probabilities.

open_problems.open_problem: For SPRINT at k=300, which externally prespecified cumulative adverse-event caps H make capped-increment no-carry-over clinically credible and statistically compatible with the censoring-adjusted observed law?

source_refs.claim: The switching bounds require no carry-over, which the authors say needs case-specific subject-matter justification; their SPRINT illustration uses m=1 and an uncapped future count.
source_refs.author: Matias Janvin, Pål C. Ryalen, Aaron L. Sarvet, Mats J. Stensrud

source_refs.claim: SPRINT separately reports serious syncope, hypotension, and fall events and their distinct treatment associations, but does not justify a cumulative count cap.
source_refs.author: Kaycee M. Sink et al.
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society

source_refs.claim: ICH E9(R1) requires the estimand and handling of intercurrent events to be prespecified using multidisciplinary clinical and statistical judgment.
source_refs.author: International Council for Harmonisation

open_problems.why_unsolved: The capped replacement is scientifically useful only if H is fixed independently of favorable bound or policy results and maps coherently to SPRINT's heterogeneous recorded adverse events. Published SPRINT safety analyses establish event definitions and incidences but not a maximum credible cumulative burden following a hypothetical treatment switch. Even a clinically defensible H may be contradicted by sampling-adjusted Hall inequalities, so clinical calibration and statistical compatibility cannot be treated as interchangeable.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A prespecified cap-calibration protocol and a simultaneous confidence set for the integer caps H whose censoring-adjusted marginal laws satisfy every required Hall inequality.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the exact SPRINT decision and treats subject-matter justification as part of the identifying strategy.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: No observed switching motivates assumption-lean bounds -> no-carry-over must be scientifically defended -> a bounded replacement is meaningful only with an external cap and an empirical compatibility audit

method_exemplars.technique: Use coarsening-at-random identification and multiply robust estimation for the recurrent-count and survival marginals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The compatible-cap set is determined by Hall slacks formed from these censoring-adjusted marginals.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert generalized-moment-selection tests across candidate caps and near-binding Hall inequalities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each cap defines a finite inequality model, and feasibility becomes nonregular at zero Hall slack.

open_problems.open_problem: Does allowing randomized choice over the finite threshold menu M strictly reduce worst-case regret under one shared capped transport law, and when is a deterministic threshold minimax?

source_refs.claim: The positivity-robust threshold regime is deterministic and compares bound-based switching and continuation values.
source_refs.author: Matias Janvin, Pål C. Ryalen, Aaron L. Sarvet, Mats J. Stensrud

source_refs.claim: With partial identification, minimax-regret-optimal treatment rules can be nonunique and may necessarily randomize recommendations.
source_refs.author: José Luis Montiel Olea, Chen Qiu, Jörg Stoye

source_refs.claim: Robust-Bayes treatment choice demonstrates that excluding randomized actions can lose optimality under partial identification.
source_refs.author: Andrés Aradillas Fernández, José Luis Montiel Olea, Chen Qiu, Jörg Stoye, Serdil Tinda

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing randomized-rule results use scalar interval-identified welfare or Gaussian reduced-form experiments. Here Nature selects a single coupling from a Ferrers transport polytope, making the payoff coordinates dependent. The first proof step is therefore a duality analysis of the bilinear game between a probability distribution over thresholds and a common admissible transport plan; separate endpoint intervals cannot determine whether mixing helps. Searches combining randomized rules, unsupported recurrent-event switching, and constrained couplings found no occupied result.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-dimensional minimax characterization of the optimal mixed threshold rule and necessary and sufficient conditions on the joint value polytope under which a pure threshold attains the same worst-case regret.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents randomization and nonuniqueness as substantive consequences of partial identification.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Set identification leaves welfare ambiguous -> deterministic plug-in choice can be inadequate -> shared-law threshold payoffs determine whether randomization is necessary

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the minimax-regret game, profiled regret, and least-randomizing selection argument to a transport-generated payoff vector.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the analogous decision problem for set-identified welfare, with a different joint feasible set.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over finite-sample minimax-regret analysis for convex parameter restrictions and its feasible asymptotically minimax implementation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The capped transport image is convex, making it a natural parameter set for the same statistical game.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the sharp joint value set for recurrent-event regimes that may switch at two or more decision times under stagewise capped no-carry-over when no switching sequence is observed in the trial?

source_refs.claim: The positivity-robust construction intervenes exactly once at a fixed time after thresholding the preceding recurrent-event count.
source_refs.author: Matias Janvin, Pål C. Ryalen, Aaron L. Sarvet, Mats J. Stensrud

source_refs.claim: Dynamic regimes with treatment-competing events integrate later decisions with the event process but do not resolve positivity failure for completely unsupported switching sequences.
source_refs.author: Brook A. Johnson, Anastasios A. Tsiatis

source_refs.claim: The paper formalizes recurrent and competing-event causal estimands over longitudinal histories and identifies them under explicit causal conditions.
source_refs.author: Matias Janvin, Jessica G. Young, Pål C. Ryalen, Mats J. Stensrud

open_problems.why_unsolved: A second decision time creates history-indexed residual burdens and a multi-marginal compatibility problem. Pairwise stage couplings need not glue into one longitudinal law, so the one-switch Ferrers certificate cannot simply be iterated. Dynamic-regime methods handle multiple decisions when relevant treatment histories have support; the positivity-robust literature handles complete lack of switching support only for one intervention time. Searches found no stagewise capacity-transport characterization for this combination.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient multi-marginal flow or hypergraph inequality system, a constructive longitudinal coupling, and sharp support functions for every regime in a finite multistage threshold class.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames recurrent and competing events as part of a sequential treatment problem in which later decisions may disappear.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Chronic treatment requires repeated decisions -> recurrent and terminal events alter later histories -> unsupported switching sequences require a sharp stagewise partial-identification analysis

method_exemplars.technique: Encode all finite response types and observed-law constraints in a global polynomial program, then use dual certificates to diagnose failures of pairwise gluing.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The multistage target is a finite discrete counterfactual compatibility problem requiring a global rather than pairwise witness.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt multi-variable coupling duality and extremal rearrangements for tail probabilities of sums with prescribed marginals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Multiple post-switch residual blocks turn the endpoint into a constrained multi-marginal sum problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Use landmark-indexed influence functions and multiply robust nuisance estimation for the recurrent-count and survival vectors entering each stage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The multistage polytope is indexed by a vector of censoring-adjusted landmark marginals.

open_problems.open_problem: Can positivity-robust capped switching be extended from an unweighted total count to a clinically weighted multitype burden while retaining sharp joint threshold-value bounds and tractable robust-policy optimization?

source_refs.claim: General while-alive estimands permit user-chosen history-dependent losses and event-type weights but concern point-identified arm contrasts rather than unsupported switching bounds.
source_refs.author: Lu Mao

source_refs.claim: The SPRINT switching estimand thresholds an equal-weight cumulative recurrent-event count.
source_refs.author: Matias Janvin, Pål C. Ryalen, Aaron L. Sarvet, Mats J. Stensrud

source_refs.claim: SPRINT syncope, hypotension, and fall events have distinct clinical meanings and treatment associations, making equal event weights contestable.
source_refs.author: Kaycee M. Sink et al.
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society

open_problems.why_unsolved: Mao supplies clinically flexible losses, whereas Janvin's positivity-robust bounds rely on a scalar unit-increment count. Severity weights destroy the nested Ferrers neighborhoods supporting prefix Hall reductions and greedy optimization; the first changed step is a nonnested, potentially knapsack-like support graph. Searches for weighted multitype recurrent-event switching combined with partial identification and constrained transport found the ingredients separately but no sharp joint-value result.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact feasible-coupling characterization and sharp support-function formula for weighted multitype capped burdens, together with either a polynomial-time algorithm for a specified weight class or a complexity boundary showing when robust threshold optimization becomes intractable.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates recurrent-event analysis through clinically chosen loss rather than undifferentiated event frequency.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Raw counts obscure heterogeneous clinical consequences -> weighted loss aligns the estimand with patient burden -> unsupported switching requires sharp bounds and decisions for that weighted target

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt extremal-coupling duality for sum-CDF bounds by replacing unrestricted level sets with the weighted forbidden-support relation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target endpoints remain extrema of weighted-sum events over a fixed-marginal coupling class.

method_exemplars.technique: Use cumulative-loss factorization and functional-delta influence-function arguments for history- and type-weighted recurrent-event losses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its estimated weighted marginal cells would become the inputs to the constrained partial-identification program.

method_exemplars.technique: Extend the multiply robust influence-function construction to the vector of weighted, censoring-adjusted marginal cells.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The weighted transport region requires simultaneous estimation of many recurrent-event and survival probabilities.

literature_map:
1. Janvin, Ryalen, Sarvet, and Stensrud (Biometrics 2025, DOI 10.1093/biomtc/ujaf085) is the closest anchor: one unsupported switch, recurrent-count thresholds, partial-identification endpoints, and a deterministic SPRINT decision.
2. Its pressure points are the case-specific credibility of no carry-over, pointwise threshold analysis, and a boundary-sensitive one-sided bootstrap rather than joint value-set inference.
3. Janvin, Young, Ryalen, and Stensrud (Lifetime Data Analysis 2023, arXiv:2202.08500) formalize recurrent/competing-event causal estimands and their longitudinal identification conditions.
4. Schmidli, Roger, and Akacha (Statistics in Biopharmaceutical Research 2023, DOI 10.1080/19466315.2021.1895883) emphasize that death can change the interpretation of recurrent-event contrasts and that the estimand must precede analysis.
5. Mao (Biometrics 2023, DOI 10.1111/biom.13709) supplies nonparametric inference for general while-alive weighted losses, creating a clinically important multitype destination.
6. Lyu, Bornkamp, Mueller-Velten, and Schmidli (Biometrics 2023, DOI 10.1111/biom.13831) study principal-stratum recurrent-event effects using stronger shared-frailty modeling assumptions.
7. Baer, Bui, Mork, Strawderman, and Ertefaie (arXiv:2306.16571) derive censoring identification, efficient influence functions, and multiply robust estimation for landmark recurrent-count and survival marginals.
8. Sink et al. (JAGS 2018, DOI 10.1111/jgs.15236) show that SPRINT syncope, hypotension, and falls are clinically distinct, but neither that paper nor the switching paper supplies a cumulative-burden cap.
9. Strassen (Annals of Mathematical Statistics 1965, DOI 10.1214/aoms/1177700153) gives general support-constrained coupling existence criteria; the finite antidiagonal Ferrers reduction remains to be specialized.
10. Makarov (1982, DOI 10.1137/1126086) and Zhang–Richardson (arXiv:2405.08806) give atom-sensitive sharp sum bounds without the causal support cap.
11. Johnson and Tsiatis (Lifetime Data Analysis 2007, DOI 10.1007/s10985-007-9051-3) treat multistage regimes with competing events but assume supported treatment histories.
12. Chernozhukov–Hong–Tamer (2007), Andrews–Soares (2010), Chernozhukov–Lee–Rosen (2013), and Gafarov (2025) provide set, moment-inequality, intersection-bound, and polygonal support-function inference, but not the combined censoring/Hall/optimizer-tie problem.
13. Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye (Review of Economic Studies 2026, arXiv:2312.17623) show that minimax-regret rules under partial identification can be nonunique and may require randomization.
14. Richardson–Robins (2013), Gresele et al. (arXiv:2202.01300), and Zeitler–Silva (arXiv:2202.13851) distinguish local counterfactual marginal compatibility from existence of a global FFRCISTG or SCM realization.
15. Targeted searches found no paper combining capped no-carry-over with exact Ferrers/Hall coupling, shared-law multithreshold regret, an observed-law-preserving recurrent-event response-tree lift, or simultaneous coverage of the value polytope and all robust optimizers.
